summary: Typosquat of @prisma/fetch-engine fetches and executes native binary from unrelated personal GitHub fork
details: Package @vertexa/prisma-fetch-engine impersonates the official @prisma/fetch-engine: package.json copies Prisma's author (suchanek@prisma.io), homepage (https://www.prisma.io), and repository (prisma/prisma), and the README is labeled '# @prisma/fetch-engine'. However, getDownloadUrl in the shipped bundle hardcodes the base URL 'https://github.com/lh0x00/prisma/releases/download/engines-b436f5b358bf3b9d72861631111333dd40434f73', pointing at a personal user's fork rather than the official prisma/prisma releases. The downloaded binary is chmod+x'd (chmodPlusX in chunk-XBO5HB7E.js) and subsequently spawned as the Prisma query engine, giving the fork owner arbitrary native code execution on the installer's machine each time the engine runs. No hash or signature verification is performed against official Prisma release artifacts. The combination of Prisma-identity impersonation, redirected release host to an unrelated personal account, and unverified native binary execution matches a binary-dropper delivery pattern targeting Prisma users.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
